title: depletion-backstop-and-thresholded-throughput-floor
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: we observed multiple incidents where aggressive warm-pool depletion (rapid lease drain + synchronous preempt) caused transient throughput collapses for a small set of tenants, increasing tail latency and customer-visible errors. Existing soft-reservation heuristics reduced impact but did not provide an operator-configurable safety net when a pool depletes faster than predictive warmup can respond.

This PR introduces a depletion-aware provisioning backstop and a thresholded throughput floor controller. The backstop operates as a conservative emergency reservation that engages when short-term depletion (1m and 5m windows) exceeds configured percentiles and predicted replenishment cannot meet the tenant's committed throughput. It is intentionally conservative: the controller holds a small backstop reservoir and enforces a per-pool minimum throughput floor until autoscaler replenishment catches up, preventing transient regressions and cascading retries.

Key changes: adds a new controller (DepletionBackstopController) in the provisioning subsystem, extends FleetConfig with backstop parameters (enabled, reservoir_size, engage_threshold_p95, min_throughput_floor_qps), emits new telemetry (depletion_rate_p95, backstop_engaged, backstop_reservoir_size), and wires the backstop into the existing LeaseAllocator so that reservations drawn from the backstop are tracked separately and reconciled during scale-up. A feature flag (provisioning.depletion_backstop) gates rollout.

Implementation notes: the controller uses an exponential decay estimator to avoid reacting to single-request bursts and performs a posterior predictive check using the last 3 minutes of depletion samples to decide engagement. When engaged it pins a lightweight floor on the allocation path (fast-path check in allocator) and tags leases with "backstop:true" so usage is visible in cost/chargeback reports. The controller is resilient to partial failures: if the backstop cannot reach the control plane (transient API error), it retries with exponential backoff and emits a distinct metric (backstop_api_retries).

Testing and perf: unit tests for the estimator, controller integration tests that simulate warm-pool drain scenarios, and a new perf canary that runs a synthetic tenant with a rapid drain profile were added. Local microbenchmarks show the allocator fast-path adds <0.3% latency at p99 under synthetic load.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag. Start with a 5% canary on dedicated pools in us-west-2 with conservative defaults (reservoir_size: 8 slots, engage_threshold_p95: 0.92, min_throughput_floor_qps: 10) for two weeks while we monitor backstop_engaged and latency regressions. Operators can tune via FleetConfig or disable entirely.

Related: ENG-9128 (incident follow-up), ENG-9147 (autoscaler stability improvements), SUP-2043 (customer ticket describing throughput collapse).

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Left a few nits on method names and one question about the decay constant default. Can we make the decay configurable?
Aisha Patel: Replied: decay constant is now configurable via FleetConfig.backstop.decay_window_seconds with a safe default (45s). Updated unit tests to cover edge cases.

Marisol Vega: Concern: allocator fast-path introduces a new branch on allocation hot path — please add microbench results.

Aisha Patel: Added microbenchmarks in the PR and included the results in the perf section of the docs. Overhead measured <0.3% at p99 under synthetic load.
Jonah Kim: Integration test flaked in CI (race between controller resume and allocator reconciliation). Recommend adding a stronger retry loop in test harness.
Aisha Patel: Added deterministic waits and a retry helper in the integration test; re-ran CI.

release_notes: Introduces an operator-configurable depletion backstop to maintain a conservative throughput floor when warm-pool depletion outpaces autoscaler replenishment. Feature is off by default and gated; metrics added: depletion_rate_p95, backstop_engaged.
